info: The gold coins of Samudragupta are important historical sources from the Gupta period. The obverse, or front side, presents the emperor as a powerful ruler, while the reverse side uses religious and artistic symbols. In this module, the coin shows Samudragupta with a bow, inscriptions written in Brahmi script, and a reverse design featuring Goddess Lakshmi seated on a lotus. The gold material reflects the wealth and economic strength of the Gupta Empire. The peacock emblem represents beauty, dignity and royalty. Together, the portrait, inscription, deity, lotus and decorative motifs help us understand Gupta kingship, religion, prosperity, art and culture.
